title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Implementing BM25 from Scratch in Python
summary: Building BM25 from scratch is like building your own bicycle before buying one at a shop. You learn every component: the wheels (inverted index), the gears (IDF weighting), the brakes (saturation), the frame (length normalisation).
objectives: ⑤ Full BM25 Implementation from Scratch

sections.title: ① Real-World Analogy
sections.body: > Building BM25 from scratch is like **building your own bicycle** before buying one at a shop. You learn every component: the wheels (inverted index), the gears (IDF weighting), the brakes (saturation), the frame (length normalisation). After you build it yourself, you'll never be confused about how any part works.

sections.title: ② Plain English Explanation
sections.body: We now have all the pieces. This lesson puts them together into one clean, complete BM25 implementation — from raw text all the way to ranked results. Every line will be commented. Nothing will be a black box.

sections.title: ③ Why Does This Matter?
sections.body: When you use a library like rank-bm25, you trust it. But when results are wrong, you don't know where to start debugging. Having built BM25 from scratch means you understand every parameter, every edge case, and can debug any issue confidently.

sections.title: ⑤ Full BM25 Implementation from Scratch
sections.body:
```python
# ============================================================
# LESSON 9: BM25 from Scratch — Complete Implementation
# 50 lines of core logic, everything commented
# ============================================================

import math
import string
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

# ── OUR 5 DOCUMENTS (same throughout all lessons) ────────────────────
documents = [
    "Python is great for machine learning and data science",        # Doc 0
    "Java is used for enterprise software development",              # Doc 1
    "Python and Java are both popular programming languages",        # Doc 2
    "Machine learning requires lots of data and computation",        # Doc 3
    "Data science uses Python for statistical analysis and modeling" # Doc 4
]

# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CLASS: BM25FromScratch
# A complete BM25 implementation — every method explained
# ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

class BM25FromScratch:
    """
    BM25 (Okapi BM25) implementation from scratch.
    
    Parameters:
        k1 (float): TF saturation parameter. Default 1.5.
                    Higher = more benefit from repeated terms.
        b  (float): Length normalisation. Default 0.75.
                    0 = ignore length, 1 = full normalisation.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, documents, k1=1.5, b=0.75):
        """
        Initialise BM25 with a list of documents.
        Builds the inverted index and computes all statistics.
        """
        self.k1 = k1
        self.b = b
        self.N = len(documents)                  # Total number of documents
        self.documents = documents
        
        # Step 1: Tokenise all documents
        self.tokenised_docs = [self._tokenise(doc) for doc in documents]
        
        # Step 2: Compute document lengths
        self.doc_lengths = [len(tokens) for tokens in self.tokenised_docs]
        
        # Step 3: Compute average document length
        self.avgdl = sum(self.doc_lengths) / self.N
        
        # Step 4: Build the inverted index (term → {doc_id: count})
        self.inverted_index = self._build_inverted_index()
        
        # Step 5: Compute document frequency for each term
        # df[term] = number of documents containing this term
        self.df = {term: len(posting) for term, posting in self.inverted_index.items()}
        
        # Step 6: Pre-compute IDF for all terms
        # (IDF doesn't change per query, so compute once)
        self.idf = {term: self._compute_idf(term) for term in self.df}
        
        print(f"BM25 index built:")
        print(f"  Documents: {self.N}")
        print(f"  Unique terms: {len(self.df)}")
        print(f"  Average doc length: {self.avgdl:.1f} words")
        print(f"  k1={self.k1}, b={self.b}")
        print()
    
    def _tokenise(self, text):
        """
        Convert raw text → list of clean lowercase tokens.
        Removes punctuation, splits on whitespace.
        """
        # Lowercase everything
        text = text.lower()
        # Remove all punctuation characters
        text = text.translate(str.maketrans('', '', string.punctuation))
        # Split on whitespace and return list of words
        return text.split()
    
    def _build_inverted_index(self):
        """
        Build inverted index: maps each term to a dict of {doc_id: count}.
        
        Example:
        {
          "python": {0: 1, 2: 1, 4: 1},
          "java":   {1: 1, 2: 1},
          ...
        }
        """
        index = defaultdict(dict)  # Automatically creates empty dicts for new keys
        
        for doc_id, tokens in enumerate(self.tokenised_docs):
            # Count occurrences of each token in this document
            token_counts = Counter(tokens)  # Counter({'python': 1, 'is': 1, ...})
            
            for term, count in token_counts.items():
                # Record: this term appears 'count' times in doc_id
                index[term][doc_id] = count
        
        return dict(index)
    
    def _compute_idf(self, term):
        """
        BM25 IDF formula:
        log( (N - df + 0.5) / (df + 0.5) + 1 )
        
        Always positive because of the +1 at the end.
        """
        doc_freq = self.df.get(term, 0)   # How many docs contain this term?
        # If term not in any doc, IDF = 0 (won't contribute to score)
        if doc_freq == 0:
            return 0.0
        return math.log((self.N - doc_freq + 0.5) / (doc_freq + 0.5) + 1)
    
    def _score_document(self, query_tokens, doc_id):
        """
        Compute BM25 score for a single document given query tokens.
        
        For each query term, computes:
        IDF(term) × [f(term,D) × (k1+1)] / [f(term,D) + k1 × length_factor]
        
        Then sums these contributions.
        """
        doc_len = self.doc_lengths[doc_id]    # Length of this specific document
        
        # Length normalisation factor
        # = 1 when doc is exactly average length
        # < 1 when doc is shorter than average (boosts score)
        # > 1 when doc is longer than average (penalises score)
        length_factor = 1 - self.b + self.b * (doc_len / self.avgdl)
        
        total_score = 0.0
        
        for term in set(query_tokens):   # 'set' avoids double-counting repeated query words
            # How many times does this query term appear in this document?
            # Look it up in the inverted index (fast!), default 0 if not found
            f = self.inverted_index.get(term, {}).get(doc_id, 0)
            
            # If term doesn't appear in document, its contribution is 0
            if f == 0:
                continue
            
            # Get pre-computed IDF for this term
            idf = self.idf.get(term, 0.0)
            
            # Compute TF component (the saturation formula)
            numerator   = f * (self.k1 + 1)
            denominator = f + self.k1 * length_factor
            tf_component = numerator / denominator
            
            # Add this term's contribution to the total score
            total_score += idf * tf_component
        
        return total_score
    
    def search(self, query, top_k=None):
        """
        Search all documents for a query and return ranked results.
        
        Args:
            query (str): The search query
            top_k (int): Return only top K results (None = return all)
        
        Returns:
            List of (doc_id, score, document_text) tuples, sorted by score descending
        """
        # Tokenise the query the same way we tokenised documents
        query_tokens = self._tokenise(query)
        
        # Score every document in our collection
        scores = []
        for doc_id in range(self.N):
            score = self._score_document(query_tokens, doc_id)
            scores.append((doc_id, score, self.documents[doc_id]))
        
        # Sort by score, highest first
        scores.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        
        # Return top_k results (or all if top_k is None)
        return scores[:top_k] if top_k else scores
    
    def get_scores(self, query):
        """
        Return BM25 scores for ALL documents (useful for debugging).
        Returns a list of scores, one per document, in doc_id order.
        """
        query_tokens = self._tokenise(query)
        return [self._score_document(query_tokens, doc_id) for doc_id in range(self.N)]
    
    def print_results(self, query, top_k=None):
        """Pretty-print search results with scores"""
        results = self.search(query, top_k=top_k)
        print(f"🔍 Query: '{query}'")
        print(f"   Tokens: {self._tokenise(query)}")
        print()
        any_results = False
        for rank, (doc_id, score, text) in enumerate(results, 1):
            if score > 0:
                any_results = True
                bar = "█" * int(score * 5)
                print(f"  Rank {rank}: [Doc {doc_id}] Score={score:.4f} {bar}")
                print(f"            '{text}'")
        if not any_results:
            print("  No matching documents found.")
        print()
    
    def show_term_details(self, query):
        """Show per-term BM25 contribution for every document"""
        query_tokens = self._tokenise(query)
        print(f"=== Term-by-Term Breakdown for Query: '{query}' ===\n")
        
        for term in set(query_tokens):
            idf = self.idf.get(term, 0)
            doc_freq = self.df.get(term, 0)
            print(f"Term: '{term}'  (df={doc_freq}, IDF={idf:.4f})")
            for doc_id in range(self.N):
                f = self.inverted_index.get(term, {}).get(doc_id, 0)
                if f > 0:
                    dl = self.doc_lengths[doc_id]
                    lf = 1 - self.b + self.b * (dl / self.avgdl)
                    tf_comp = (f * (self.k1 + 1)) / (f + self.k1 * lf)
                    contrib = idf * tf_comp
                    print(f"  Doc {doc_id}: f={f}, len={dl}, TF_comp={tf_comp:.4f}, contribution={contrib:.4f}")
            print()

# ── INSTANTIATE AND TEST ──────────────────────────────────────────────

print("=" * 65)
print("           BM25 FROM SCRATCH — FULL TEST")
print("=" * 65)
print()

# Create BM25 index with our 5 documents
bm25 = BM25FromScratch(documents, k1=1.5, b=0.75)

# ── TEST QUERY 1 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
bm25.print_results("python machine learning")

# ── TEST QUERY 2 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
bm25.print_results("enterprise software development")

# ── TEST QUERY 3 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
bm25.print_results("data science analysis")

# ── TERM-BY-TERM BREAKDOWN ────────────────────────────────────────────
bm25.show_term_details("python data")

# ── SHOW RAW SCORES ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("=== Raw Scores for 'python machine learning' ===")
scores = bm25.get_scores("python machine learning")
for doc_id, score in enumerate(scores):
    print(f"  Doc {doc_id}: {score:.4f}")
```

sections.title: ⑥ Common Beginner Mistakes
sections.body:
❌ **Mistake 1:** Using a list instead of a set for query tokens — duplicate query words get double-counted
✅ **Fix:** Use `set(query_tokens)` when iterating over query terms in the scoring loop

❌ **Mistake 2:** Not using `defaultdict` — forgetting to initialise leads to `KeyError`
✅ **Fix:** Use `defaultdict(dict)` for the inverted index

❌ **Mistake 3:** Computing IDF inside the scoring loop (slow!) — it's the same for every query
✅ **Fix:** Pre-compute IDF once during `__init__` and cache it

❌ **Mistake 4:** Forgetting to apply `_tokenise` to the query — searching for "Python" when index has "python"
✅ **Fix:** Always tokenise both documents AND queries with the exact same function

❌ **Mistake 5:** Returning only docs with score > 0, missing edge cases
✅ **Fix:** Return all docs with their scores; let the caller decide the threshold

sections.title: ⑦ Quick Recap
sections.body:
- 🏗️ Build BM25 in 6 steps: tokenise → invert index → compute lengths → compute IDF → score → rank
- 🔑 Pre-compute IDF and avgdl **once** at index time, not per query
- 📋 The inverted index lets you look up term frequency per document in O(1)
- 🎯 `set(query_tokens)` prevents double-counting repeated query words
- 🔧 The `_score_document` function is the heart — everything else supports it
